sentences.text: The skull of this dinosaur featured a relatively deep snout, a trait suggested by the square shape of its premaxilla bone.
Its nostrils sat near the tip of the snout, while a large, circular eye socket resembled that of the early dinosaur Eoraptor.
Four teeth lined each side of the premaxilla bone in the upper jaw.
Two bony shelves extended from the inner wall of the premaxilla, stacked one above the other.
These stacked shelves are distinctive characteristics that separate this genus from its related sauropodomorph relatives.
The nasal bone was plate-like and bore four extensions, with two pointing forward and two pointing backward.
Unlike the triangular shape found in most related genera, the lower forward extension of the nasal bone was tongue-shaped and broader than the upper one.
The postorbital bone formed the upper rear corner of the eye socket and carried three large processes extending forward, downward, and backward.
A fourth small process on this bone pointed upward and inward to join the parietal bone, an orientation unique among dinosaurs.
The backward-pointing process of the postorbital bone ended in a split tip rather than tapering to a point, differing from most basal sauropodomorphs.
The presence of two right nasal bones suggests that at least two individuals lived at the fossil site.
Small body size and open bone sutures indicate that the discovered specimens were likely juveniles.
Detailed analysis proved these fossils did not belong to the species Aardonyx or Massospondylus.
Adam Yates, Matthew Bonnan, and Johann Neveling first named the dinosaur in 2011.
The genus name Arcusaurus derives from the Latin word for 'rainbow', referencing the Rainbow Nation.
The species name honors Lucille Pereira and Fernando Abdala, who found the fossils.
Fossils were collected in March 2006 from the Spion Kop Heelbo site in Senekal, Free State, South Africa.
The holotype specimen, which serves as the basis for the species description, is a partial skull cataloged as BP/1/6235.
The close relationship between Arcusaurus and the Late Triassic dinosaur Efraasia implies a 35-million-year ghost lineage for sauropodomorphs.
Phylogenetic studies classify Arcusaurus as a basal sauropodomorph, placing it as a sister group to Efraasia and more derived sauropodomorphs.
It is debated whether Arcusaurus belongs with basal sauropodomorphs, as it possesses unique features of the advanced clade Plateosauria that raise doubts about phylogenetic results.
Arcusaurus lived in South Africa during the Early Jurassic period, specifically the Pliensbachian stage.
The time range for Arcusaurus is estimated to be between 201.4 and 192.9 million years ago.
